consensus_summary: Name primarily symbolizes the essential character, nature, identity, authority, presence, and reputation of the bearer (especially God), so the name stands for the person; common secondary facets include delegated authority, renown, covenant belonging/ownership, and new-name identity transformation.
book_summary: Name is the covenant itself, taken as a bride takes her husband’s name; to be called by His name is to be brought under His protective wing (covering), whose corners carry the reminder of the commandments.
consensus_core_identification: the character, identity, authority, presence, and reputation of the person (esp. God)
book_core_identification: the covenant itself (bridal taking of the name under protective wing-covering linked to the commandments)
boundary_disagreement: Book makes the primary sense the marriage-covenant covering (with wing/commandment imagery) and thus restricts central cases to covenantal belonging/protection; consensus treats character/identity/authority as primary across far broader usage, with covenant belonging only a secondary facet.
material_contradiction: None; the book explicitly notes the common teaching of character/authority/reputation and the two can stand as complementary layers or emphases rather than mutually exclusive claims.
rationale: Both cores operate inside the same broad category (name as marker of one’s identification with/relationship to God, including belonging and protection). The book therefore does not replace the referent or invent an uncovered one; it preserves the category while materially narrowing the primary identification to ‘the covenant itself’ via bridal-wing imagery and re-centering the extension on those specific cases, producing a real boundary refinement rather than equivalence, contradiction, or novelty.
strongest_objection: Broad scriptural patterns of divine self-revelation, hallowing, and exaltation of the name more naturally support character/identity/authority as primary; the book’s covenant-bridal reading (and the unstated kanaf–tzitzit link) is a specialized application of a few texts rather than the core sense.
